raw_response:
I'm a 65-year-old cotton farmer in Quzhou County with 42 years under my belt and an agricultural college education from back in the early 1980s. My wife and I work these 15 mu together — just the two of us now, since our children moved to the city years ago. At my age, I know the science, but I've also learned that on a small farm, every jiao matters. I can't afford to chase theoretical yields if it means emptying my pocket on inputs that might not pay back.

I planted cotton because it suits my land and my labor situation. With only two of us, wheat-maize double cropping is too rushed and too exhausting — the turnaround between wheat harvest and maize planting would kill my back, and I'd need to hire machinery I can't justify on 15 mu. Cotton gives me a longer season with more flexible labor demands, though the picking in autumn is still heavy work.

This year I'll plant my usual improved cotton variety in mid-to-late April, once the soil warms up properly. I saved some seed from last year but I'll buy fresh certified seed for about 80 yuan per mu — saved seed loses vigor and the 1,200 yuan total is worth it for the germination rate. I'll plow and harrow the fields in early April, same as always.

For fertilizer, I know the soil tests would tell me to aim for 18 kg N per mu, but testing costs 200 yuan and I can read my fields well enough after four decades. I'll apply 40 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as a base before planting — that gives me 6 kg each of N, P₂O₅, and K₂O per mu. Then at early flowering in July, I'll topdress with 20 kg per mu of urea, which adds another 9.2 kg N. Total nitrogen is about 15 kg per mu. I could push it to 18 kg, but urea prices are up and I'd rather have 500 yuan in my pocket for emergencies than gamble on an extra 3 kg of nitrogen that might not matter if July turns dry again.

I'll irrigate three times using my tube well: once at planting if the spring is dry, once at flowering in July, and once at boll filling in August. Electricity for pumping isn't cheap anymore, so I won't water unless the top 10 cm of soil is genuinely dry. Three times is enough for cotton on this soil if I'm careful.

Pesticides — cotton bollworm is my main enemy here. I'll spray insecticide twice during the season, and I'll apply herbicide once before planting to control weeds. Hand-weeding 15 mu is impossible with just two of us, especially at my age. The pesticide bill adds up, but losing half the crop to bollworm would be devastating.

Labor is my tightest constraint. My wife and I will put in about 75 days of family labor over the season — planting, managing, spraying, and some early picking. But when the bolls open in September and October, we'll need to pick three or four times. I'll hire about 12 days of seasonal labor for the peak picking periods at roughly 140 yuan per day. Even that hurts the budget, but my hands and back can't do it all anymore.

I'm targeting about 280 kg of lint cotton per mu this year. Last year I managed 260 kg/mu because a dry July stressed the plants at flowering. The spring looks normal so far, and my irrigation should cover the critical periods. I won't let greed push me to spend more — 280 kg/mu on 15 mu at current prices will keep us comfortable without taking risks we can't afford.
